medications.duration: Lifelong — review after 4 weeks, then titrate to target and review annually
medications.purpose: Initial blood pressure control as first-line therapy for hypertension
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG136 recommends an ACE inhibitor as first-line treatment for patients <55 years and not of Afro‑Caribbean origin (step 1) and advises monitoring renal function and potassium after initiation.

contraindications.reason: Potential teratogenicity; contraindicated if patient is pregnant or planning pregnancy (NICE NG136).
contraindications.alternative: Defer ACE‑I until pregnancy status is confirmed; consider alternative antihypertensive such as labetalol if immediate treatment is required.

assumptions_warnings: Patient age and ethnicity not recorded; ACE‑I chosen assuming age <55 and non‑Afro‑Caribbean per NICE NG136.
Baseline eGFR and serum potassium not available; ACE‑I initiation requires renal function and potassium assessment.
Pregnancy status unknown; ACE‑I contraindicated in pregnancy per NICE NG136.
QRISK cardiovascular risk score not calculated; needed to assess need for statin therapy.
Lifestyle factors (smoking, alcohol intake, BMI) not documented; counseling on salt restriction, weight management, exercise, smoking cessation, and alcohol moderation is recommended.
treatment_summary: Start ramipril 2.5 mg once daily as first-line antihypertensive therapy, obtain baseline renal function and electrolytes, confirm pregnancy status, and arrange BP review in 4 weeks with titration to 5‑10 mg as needed. Provide lifestyle advice (salt <6 g/day, weight control, regular exercise, smoking cessation, limit alcohol) and arrange QRISK assessment and CPAP evaluation for obstructive sleep apnea.
